description: The 1-bend visibility graph search finds a short orthogonal route, made of horizontal and vertical segments, with few bends. Its nodes are the ports and the obstacle corners, each corner with a heading along one of its sides. An edge joins two nodes when a path with at most one bend connects them. A* over this graph tries only routes that hug obstacles, and the paper proves that one of them is optimal for length and bends. In `connector-routing` it is opt-in (`Search::OneBend`), because tests found a narrow slit where it misses the optimum.

papers.authors: Kim Marriott, Peter J. Stuckey, Michael Wybrow
papers.title: Seeing Around Corners: Fast Orthogonal Connector Routing

lineage.source: connector-routing, src/search/one_bend.rs: "successors are generated by walking the orthogonal visibility graph from the node along its heading"
connector-routing, src/search.rs: "A* over the lazily generated 1-bend visibility graph (Marriott et al. 2014)"
